questions.question: The area of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal box is 120 cm² , 72 cm² and 60 cm² , respectively. Find the volume (in cm³ ) of the box.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal box:

 
• Area 1 = 120 cm²
 
• Area 2 = 72 cm²
 
• Area 3 = 60 cm²

**Formula used:**

Volume of cuboid = √(Area 1 × Area 2 × Area 3)

Let the dimensions of the cuboid be l, b, and h. We have:

 
• l × b = 120
 
• b × h = 72
 
• h × l = 60

Volume of the cuboid (V) = l × b × h = √(l × b × b × h × h × l)

**Calculation:**

V = √(120 × 72 × 60)

⇒ V = √518400

⇒ V = 720 cm³

**∴ The volume of the cuboid is 720 cm³.**

questions.question: A solid metallic ball of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into a right circular cylinder of double the radius of the ball. The curved surface area of the cylinder is:

Concept:

The cylinder would be cast from the ball. Hence, the volume of cylinder would be equal to the volume of the ball.

Formula:

Volume of cylinder = π × r2 × h

CSA = 2πrh, where-

CSA = Curved Surface Area

r = radius of cylinder

h = height of cylinder

Volume of solid ball = 4over3 × π × R3

R = Radius of the solid ball

Calculation:

Radius of cylinder = 2 × 9 = 18 cm

Volume of cylinder = π × 18 × 18 × h = 324πh cm3

Volume of solid ball = 4over3 × π × 9 × 9 × 9 = 972π cm3

According to the question-

Volume of cylinder = Volume of solid ball

⇒ 324πh = 972π

⇒ h = 3 cm

∴ CSA = 2 × π × 18 × 3 = 108π cm2

∴ **The Curved Surface Area of the cylinder is 108π cm2**

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a rectangular box are in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 4 respectively and the cost of covering it with a sheet of paper at the rate of Rs. 1.50 per square metre is Rs. 1,950. Find the volume of the box.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length, breadth and height of a rectangular box are in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 4 respectively

Cost of covering it at the rate of Rs. 1.50 per square metre = Rs. 1,950

**Formula used:**

The total surface area of a rectangular box = 2 (length × breadth + breadth × height + height × length)

The volume of a rectangular box = length × breadth × height

**Calculation: **

Let the length, breadth and height of a rectangular box be 3x, 2x and 4x respectively.

The total surface area of a rectangular box = 2[(3x × 2x) + (2x × 4x) + (4x × 3x)]

⇒ 2 × (6x² + 8x² + 12x²)

⇒ 2 × 26x²

⇒ 52x²

Total cost for covering it at the rate of Rs. 1.5 per square metre = Rs. 1,950

⇒ 52x² × 1.5 = 1,950

⇒ x² = 1950/(52 × 1.5)

⇒ x² = 25

⇒ x = 5 metres

Then, length = 3x

⇒ 3 × 5

⇒ 15 metres

Breadth = 2x

⇒ 2 × 5

⇒ 10 metres

Height = 4x

⇒ 4 × 5

⇒ 20 metres

The volume of a rectangular box = 15 × 10 × 20

⇒ 3000 m³

**∴ The volume of rectangular box is 3000 m³**

questions.question: The number of balls, each one is 4 cm in the diameter that can be made from a solid metallic sphere of diameter 32 cm is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The diameter of each small ball = 4 cm

Diameter of a large sphere = 32 cm

**Formula:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(r³)

**Calculation:**

Radius of small ball = 4 cm / 2 = 2 cm

Radius of large sphere = 32 cm / 2 = 16 cm

The volume of small ball ⇒ (4/3)π(2³) = (4/3)π(8) = (32/3)π cm³

The Volume of large sphere ⇒ (4/3)π(16³) = (4/3)π(4096) = (16384/3)π cm³

Number of small balls = Volume of large sphere / Volume of small ball

⇒ (16384/3)π / (32/3)π = 16384 / 32 = 512

**So, 512 small balls can be made.**

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a hall are 10 m, 20 m and 15 m respectively. Find the cost of whitewashing the walls of the inside of the hall and ceiling at the rate of Rs. 10.20/m²

questions.question: If three spheres of radius 75 cm, 60 cm and 45 cm are melted into one big sphere, then the radius of the big sphere is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

radius of there sphere are 75cm, 60cm and 45 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = 4/3 πr³

a³ + b³ + c³ = 1/2 (a + b + c)[(a - b)² + (b - c)² + (c - a)²] + 3abc

**Calculation:**

Volume of new sphere = Sum of volume of all three sphere

⇒ 4/3 πR³ = 4/3 π(75)³ + 4/3 π(60)³ + 4/3 π(45)³

⇒ 4/3 πR3 = 4/3 π [75³ + 60³ + 45³]

⇒ R³ = [753 + 603 + 453]

⇒ R3 = 1/2 × (75 + 60 + 45) [(75 - 60)² + (60 - 45)² + (45 - 75)²] + 3 × 75 × 60 × 45

⇒ R3 = 1/2 × 180 [15² + 15² + 30²] + 3 × 75 × 60 × 45

⇒ R3 = 90 × (225 + 225 + 900) + 3 × 75 × 60 × 45

⇒ R3 = 90 [1350 + 6750]

⇒ R3 = 90 × 8100

⇒ R3 = 90 × 90 × 90

⇒ R = 90 cm

**Hence, the radius of the big sphere is 90 cm.**

questions.question: A rectangular piece of paper is 50 cm long and 22 cm wide. If a cylinder is formed by rolling the paper along its breadth, then the volume of the cylinder is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When rolled along its breadth, Breadth (B) = Circumference, and Length (L) = Height.

Direct formula for Volume = (B² × L) ÷ 4π

Volume = (22 × 22 × 50 × 7) ÷ (4 × 22)

Volume = 7700 ÷ 4 = 1925 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f04c7b44d5ff43c7f6796feb371b0dd52694522517860d696e37db25cb2be686.png] 

**Given:**

Length of paper (l) = 50 cm

Breadth of paper (b) = 22 cm

When the rectangular sheet is rolled along its breadth:

Circumference of the cylinder's base = 22 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 50 cm

**Formula Used:**

Circumference = 2πr

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 22

⇒ r = (22 × 7) ÷ (2 × 22)

⇒ r = 3.5 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 50

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) × 50

⇒ Volume = 11 × 7 × 25

⇒ Volume = 1925 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rolling a Rectangular Sheet

When rolled along its length, the length forms the circumference and the breadth becomes the height. When rolled along its breadth, the breadth forms the circumference and the length becomes the height.

Surface Areas of a Cylinder

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) is given by 2πrh, and the Total Surface Area (TSA) is 2πr(h + r), where r is the radius and h is the height.

Relationship with Cone

A cylinder and a cone with the same base radius and height have volumes in the ratio 3:1. The volume of the cone is 1/3 × πr²h.

questions.question: A metallic sphere of volume 3136 π cm³ is melted and then, recast into smaller cones, each of radius 3.5 cm and height 4 cm. How many cones are obtained?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A metallic sphere of volume 3136 π cm³ is melted and recast into smaller cones, each of radius 3.5 cm and height 4 cm.

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = Volume of cone × Number of cones

Volume of sphere = (4)/(3)pi r³

Volume of cone = (1)/(3)pi r²h

**Calculation:**

Given volume of sphere = 3136 π cm³

Radius of cone (r) = 3.5 cm

Height of cone (h) = 4 cm

Volume of one cone = (1)/(3)pi (3.5)² times 4

⇒ Volume of one cone = (1)/(3)pi times 12.25 times 4

⇒ Volume of one cone = (1)/(3) times 49pi

⇒ Volume of one cone = 16.33 π cm³

Number of cones = (Volume of sphere)/(Volume of one cone)

⇒ Number of cones = (3136pi)/(16.33pi)

⇒ Number of cones = 192

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The circumference of base of a right circular cone is 88 cm. If the height of the cone is 28 cm, then what is the curved surface area of the cone?

The slant height (ℓ) of the cone is given by:

ℓ² = r² + h²

ℓ² = 14² + 28²

ℓ² = 980

ℓ = √980 = 14√5 cm

Now, we can use the formula for the curved surface area of a cone:

The curved surface area of the cone = πrℓ

= 22\7 × (14)(14√5)

= 616√5 

**Therefore, the curved surface area of the cone is 616√5 cm².**
